findings.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model
findings.summary_md: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28, 2026 as its strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities, ranking first on the Artificial Analysis index at 59 and leading SEC-bench Pro (88.2%), ExploitGym (54.8%), and CWE-bench (71.0%). The model was initially released to a subset of cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, with broader availability to developers, businesses, and consumers promised later. Google said Wiz observed Carbon leading on web penetration-testing benchmarks and that the Chrome team saw Carbon perform more than 10x better than another lab's large frontier model when generating high-quality patches.

findings.title: Google Says Gemini 4 Carbon Leads in Finding, Exploiting and Fixing Vulnerabilities
findings.summary_md: SecurityWeek reported that Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier AI model that, according to the company, beats rival models on benchmarks for detecting, exploiting, and patching vulnerabilities. The article noted the model's initial restriction to vetted cyber defenders through Google's Fairwind Program. It represents the first news coverage of the Carbon announcement.

findings.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code Formally Verifies Signal Protocol Guarantees in Four Weeks
findings.summary_md: Google DeepMind introduced AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent AI framework for formal software specification and verification, and applied it to libsignal, the Signal protocol's reference implementation. Agents powered by Gemini Carbon generated over six million lines of Lean proof in four weeks to verify key security properties of the compiled code, work that historically takes expert teams years. To confirm the system could distinguish correct from buggy code, researchers reintroduced two real, previously fixed bugs into an isolated version of Signal's code and the system produced machine-checked proofs that the buggy versions were insecure. Signal CTO Ehren Kret called the approach a major breakthrough.

findings.title: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code Formally Verifies Signal Protocol Guarantees in Four Weeks - AI Weekly
findings.summary_md: AI Weekly covered Google DeepMind's announcement that AlphaProof Code formally verified Signal protocol guarantees, noting that DeepMind open-sourced the specification and proofs. The article framed the work as the first formal verification of a widely deployed cryptographic protocol's implementation. It appeared ahead of the story's ingestion time.

findings.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
findings.summary_md: Google announced that Gemini 4 Carbon is now available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers via the Gemini API and Gemini for business, with Google AI Ultra subscribers also receiving access. Introductory pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens applies until November 30, 2026, after which prices double to $4 and $20. Google disclosed that its Cloud Vulnerability Research team used Carbon to prove two bugs in a popular open-source project were exploitable, with severity comparable to PHP2Shell, and that Wiz found zero-day vulnerabilities at two major SaaS providers in under two hours using Carbon for cyber. Fairwind membership remains required for Carbon for cyber.

findings.title: Limited reports of PHP bug exploitation emerge
findings.summary_md: The Record reported that cybersecurity firm GreyNoise observed at least six successful exploitations of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, known as PHP2Shell, after the bugs were added to the U.S. KEV catalog. GreyNoise recorded the first successful exploitation on October 28, 2026 at 05:14:01 UTC. The bugs are the pair Google later cited as comparable in severity to the two open-source bugs its Cloud Vulnerability Research team confirmed with Carbon.
